name: Tanzania

findings.local_actor: Tanzania Telecommunications Company Ltd (TTCL), backbone manager
findings.builder: Huawei; China International Telecommunication Construction Corporation (CITCC)
findings.summary: Huawei and CITCC built Phase II of the National ICT Broadband Backbone (about 3,230 km) on a RMB700m China Exim concessional loan, completed 2015; a Phase III loan added Zanzibar links and an IP-MPLS layer, operational September 2016.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: AidData records Huawei and CITCC as contractors for Phase II; Phase III contractor not confirmed in this pass. Pole prc because Huawei supplies the transmission equipment and firmware. AidData converts the RMB700m commitment to about US$133m (constant 2023 USD), not used as announced value. The 2023 Huawei extension (TZA-002) suggests the backbone remains in service, but current status was not confirmed directly, so still_current is null. Audit 2026-10-25: newer information - AidData: Phase II 3,230 km laid, completed 21 Oct 2015; Phase III separate US$93.77m loan signed 25 Mar 2013 (Zanzibar/Pemba, IP-MPLS, Dar es Salaam data centre), NICTBB operational Sept 2016.

findings.summary: TTCL signed a US$15.9m agreement with Huawei's local subsidiary to extend the national broadband backbone by 1,520 km to 23 more districts within six months.
findings.analyst_inference: Financing for the extension not stated in the opened source. Completion not confirmed.

findings.summary: Vodacom Tanzania is replacing its Nokia radio access network with Huawei equipment in a major rip-and-replace; a US$100m+ modernisation had upgraded over 1,000 sites by September 2025, with Huawei named as supplier.
findings.analyst_inference: Vodacom group CEO attributed the swap to a more attractive Huawei offer (commercial). The TelcoTitans article is paywalled and undated; the two September 2025 reports name Huawei only for energy-saving radio technology and do not state Huawei supplies the whole $100m programme, so the two claims are linked by inference and corroborated is left false. Tier 4 because rollout is under way (1,000+ sites), not complete. Audit 2026-10-25: partly supported - TelcoTitans (undated, paywalled, apparently Huawei-sourced) supports a Nokia-to-Huawei RAN rip-and-replace being initiated but gives no sites, cost or status. Tech In Africa names Huawei only as supplier of energy-saving radio tech and does not mention Nokia, so tying the US$100m+ programme and 1,000+ sites to the Huawei swap (and announced_value_usd) is inference. techafricanews URL did not appear in search; not fetched.

findings.reversal_of: Nokia radio access network at Vodacom Tanzania
findings.summary: Vodacom Tanzania's Nokia radio access network equipment is being removed and replaced by Huawei equipment.
findings.analyst_inference: Reversal of installed Nokia (Finland) RAN, so tier 5 is the tier of the thing reversed. Coded commercial because the stated driver is Huawei's price offer, not security policy; it does not move the map. Date approximate: the article is undated, listed among items from 2025.

findings.summary: Tigo Tanzania and Ericsson announced a multi-year deal: Ericsson upgrades the 4G radio and microwave network, supplies 5G radios (live in Dar es Salaam, Dodoma, Zanzibar) and AI optimisation software.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third. Value undisclosed; core network vendor not stated. Tigo Tanzania was rebranded Yas under Madagascar's Axian group; whether the Ericsson deal continues post-rebrand was not checked.

findings.summary: TTCL signed a ten-year partnership with Huawei to launch a 4.5G network; Huawei has also served as the government's official ICT adviser under a 2015 cooperation agreement.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 because it is a long-term partnership with no value or rollout terms disclosed. Pre-2020 and current status unconfirmed, so still_current is null. DCD corroborates the Huawei adviser role, Ecofin the 4.5G partnership.

findings.controller: Government of Tanzania (Ministry of Communications) / TTCL
findings.local_actor: National Internet Data Centre, Dar es Salaam
findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (NICTBB Phase III loan, per AidData)
findings.summary: The government announced a US$93.6m national data centre with Huawei as ICT adviser and bandwidth provider; AidData records a China Exim-funded NICTBB Phase III data centre in Dar es Salaam, operational 2016.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary), Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is the Tanzanian state, so domestic; Huawei's role as builder or IT-equipment supplier is likely but not stated in the opened sources, so builder is null. Linking DCD's US$93.6m centre to AidData's Phase III data centre is an inference; the China Exim financier rests on AidData only. If Huawei IT equipment runs it, a separate prc equipment finding would apply.

findings.summary: Raxio is building TZ1, a 6 MW, 800-rack carrier-neutral Tier III colocation facility outside Dar es Salaam, planned to launch in 2026; backers Meridiam and Roha raised its funding pool to US$380m.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: Raxio is a pan-African operator whose headquarters and controlling shareholder were not established; its backers are Roha (an Africa-focused US investment firm) and Meridiam (French), so control is foreign but could be us or third. Tier 2 because launch is planned but construction status and opening are not confirmed; originally slated for 2023, so the project has slipped.

findings.controller: Government of Tanzania (Ministry of Communication and Information Technology)
findings.summary: The communications minister said Tanzania is preparing to establish AI data centres and is assessing required infrastructure; no site, budget, partner or timeline was given.
findings.analyst_inference: State-owned newspaper relaying a minister's statement, so S4. Controller provisionally domestic as a government plan; the actual builder, operator and equipment stack are unknown.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
findings.summary: The communications ministry signed an MOU with Huawei Technologies Tanzania in Shanghai covering AI application, ICT infrastructure, digital public service infrastructure, local skills and device assembly and repair.
findings.analyst_inference: Signed in Shanghai around the WAICO founding period (Tanzania acceded 31 July 2026 per global layer), which suggests a diplomatic package, but no bundle link is documented. Non-binding MOU; no projects or values named. A June 2025 Citizen headline says Huawei committed to modernising public services (body not readable).

findings.summary: Tanzania plans to install 6,500 AI-equipped security cameras across Dar es Salaam, Dodoma, Arusha and Mwanza in commercial areas, streets and public gathering sites; no vendor, value or timeline was reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null because no vendor is named; only the article summary was readable. Whether Huawei, Hikvision, Dahua or another supplier is involved is a research gap.

silicon.null_reason: search budget spent on networks, facilities and applications; no accelerator purchases or export licences surfaced incidentally

models.null_reason: one search on government AI partnerships found only the July 2026 Huawei MOU (coded under applications) and AI-data-centre plans; no frontier-model partnership or sovereign Tanzanian model found

corrections.note: Weekly audit 2026-10-25: 7 selected finding(s) source-checked by independent checkers; corrections from pages the checkers read (dates, summaries, still_current, newer information, added opened sources) and spec-required recoding.

research_gaps: Date, scope and site count of Vodacom Tanzania's Nokia-to-Huawei RAN swap (TelcoTitans article paywalled and undated); does Huawei also supply Vodacom's core?
RAN/core vendors for Airtel Tanzania, Halotel (Viettel) and TTCL mobile; whether Yas (ex-Tigo) kept Ericsson after the Axian rebrand.
Contractor, IT-equipment vendor and current operator of the National Internet Data Centre; whether it hosts government cloud on Huawei stack.
Vendor and status of the 6,500-camera AI surveillance plan (2024) and any earlier Dar es Salaam police CCTV systems.
Raxio TZ1: controlling shareholder/headquarters (sets pole), construction status and opening; IFC US$100m loan (2024, ippmedia headline only).
Wing Africa US$50m data centre launched in Dar es Salaam March 2025 (The Citizen): owner nationality, capacity, status.
What, if any, projects followed the July 2026 Huawei MOU and the June 2025 Huawei public-services commitment; any links to WAICO accession.
Did the 2023 TTCL-Huawei backbone extension complete, and who financed it?
Halotel (Viettel, Vietnam) network vendor and any 2G/3G/4G build by Huawei or ZTE.
